subject: EdgeHealth expansion: midcycle capacity, pricing framework and co-term path
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@edgehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@edgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity increase and co-term option

Hi Mina,

Quick note after our internal planning: we expect a 2.8x spike in inference usage for our provider-matching pipeline starting mid-September (pilot finishes Aug 25). We want to expand committed capacity now rather than wait for renewal to avoid burst pricing.

Questions:
- Can Redwood provide a midcycle top-up that can be co-termed to our March 2027 renewal?
- What discount / rate cadence would apply for a mid-contract committed add-on?
- Any options to annualize pricing (spread impact over invoices) to keep finance predictable?

We have procurement on copy — they will need a commercial framework and a short MOP (mutual action plan). Can Alex share a simple proposal and a straw-man discount matrix?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeHealth
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity increase and co-term option

Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the timing.

Alex — looping you in to propose a clear path. High-level thoughts from product/finance here (Marissa copied for approval on the asked discount bands):
- We can offer a midcycle committed top-up and align its term to co-term on 2027-03-31 (co-terming to renewal).
- Two commercial choices: (A) One-off top-up with pro-rated pricing + preservation of existing unit rate; (B) Upgrade to a blended committed bucket priced at a reduced blended unit rate (requires committing to new total for remainder of the term).
- We can offer an annualization option: spread the incremental charge across remaining invoices as a monthly amortization (finance-friendly) — requires signed amendment and PO.

Deliverables I propose: 1) Alex to send a short proposal (PDF) with two priced scenarios + straw-man discounts for committed uplift tiers; 2) simple MAP with dates and procurement items.

Marissa — can you confirm an internal approval threshold for a discount >12% so Alex knows if he needs escalation?

Mina
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: usage_rollforward_Q2-2026.csv (CSV)
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@edgehealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@edgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: EdgeHealth — midcycle expansion proposal (two scenarios)

Samantha / team,

Appended below are two concise scenarios — full line-item proposal attached (EdgeHealth_renewal_proposal_v3.pdf). I kept assumptions visible so procurement can review quickly.

Assumptions:
- Current committed monthly token equivalent: 10M inference units.
- Forecasted incremental need: +18M units/month starting 2026-09-15 (pilot ramp to prod).
- Remaining term length if co-term to 2027-03-31: ~8 months.

Scenario A — Top-up (fast path)
- Add-on committed block: +18M units/month for remainder of term (8 months).
- Rate: current list unit rate, pro-rated for 8 months.
- Discount: 5% on the incremental block if signed amendment within 10 business days.
- Billing: single one-time invoice or optional monthly amortization.

Scenario B — Blended re-commit (preferred for unit economics)
- Re-commit to total 28M units/month for remainder of term, blended unit rate across whole committed volume.
- Proposed blended discount tiers (by uplift % over base):
  - +50–100% uplift: 10% blended discount
  - +100–200% uplift: 14% blended discount
  - >200% uplift: 18% blended discount (requires CFO approval)
- Billing: immediate amendment; we can amortize incremental delta across remaining invoices to smooth finance impact.

Next steps:
1) If procurement wants the fast path, confirm Scenario A and I’ll send a short amendment for signatures.
2) If you prefer better unit economics, signal Scenario B and provide a quick usage commitment and we’ll route for Marissa’s pricing check.

Attachments: EdgeHealth_renewal_proposal_v3.pdf (PDF)

Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@edgehealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@edgehealth.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@edgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeHealth — midcycle expansion proposal (two scenarios)

Alex / Mina — thanks for the clear options. Procurement prefers Scenario B (blended re-commit) so we can lock a predictable unit cost. We have two asks before routing to finance:

1) Can Redwood confirm the blended rate calculation example for the 28M total (show math and resulting monthly invoice impact)?
2) Given our org constraints, we’d like the amortization path: split the delta across the 8 remaining invoices rather than a single invoice. Will the amendment and co-term paperwork be simple (single-signature amendment + PO)?

If you can send the numeric worked example and a draft amendment by EOD Friday (2026-08-06), procurement will start the PO path.

Ben Ortiz
Finance Ops, EdgeHealth
